meta.experiment: Experiment 05 — Flight Control System: PID Tuning, Ziegler–Nichols & Sensor Fusion
meta.configuration: Quadcopter attitude loop (roll axis) — cascaded angle + rate control with complementary-filter attitude estimation
meta.note: Control-systems component database. Gains: Kp [N·m/rad], Ki [N·m/(rad·s)], Kd [N·m·s/rad]. Inertia J in kg·m². Time constants in seconds. Angles in degrees unless a formula states radians. The default 5-inch airframe (J = 0.003 kg·m²) reproduces every worked example in theory.md. Roll inertia is computed from the Experiment-2 build via J = m·L²/2 (mass lumped at the four motor positions of an X-quad), so the airframe inherited from upstream drives the dynamics.

airframes.label: 3" Toothpick
airframes.note: Ultralight micro. Tiny inertia -> very fast loop, high bandwidth, but twitchy and noise-sensitive.

airframes.label: 5" Freestyle (reference)
airframes.note: The reference airframe used in every theory.md worked example. J = m·L²/2 = 0.5·0.110²/2 = 0.00303 ≈ 0.003 kg·m². Rate-loop lags give Ku = 19.25, Pu = 0.0513 s.

airframes.label: 7" Cinematic
airframes.note: Heavier, larger inertia -> slower attitude response; needs higher Kp for the same bandwidth.

airframes.label: 10" Heavy-Lift
airframes.note: Large platform. High inertia and slow actuators force conservative gains and a long settling time.

inertia_model.description: Roll-axis moment of inertia estimated from the physical build inherited from Experiment 2. For an X-configuration quad the four motors sit at arm radius L, each 45° from the roll axis (perpendicular distance L/√2). Lumping the mass at the motors: J = 4·(m/4)·(L/√2)² = m·L²/2.
inertia_model.note: Upper-bound estimate (all mass at the motor positions). Real builds carry central mass closer to the axis, so the true J is somewhat lower; the model is documented as an approximation in theory.md (Limitation 1).

plant.description: Two-loop attitude model. (a) Angle loop: PD control of the rigid-body integrator, torque->angle = 1/(J·s²); the closed loop is the prototype 2nd-order system. (b) Rate loop: a Type-0 chain of three first-order lags (mechanical, actuator, sensor) on which Ziegler–Nichols' ultimate-gain method has a finite, well-defined Ku.
plant.note: A pure 1/(J s²) plant oscillates at EVERY proportional gain (poles sit on the jω axis), so its ultimate gain is undefined — that is why the lag model is required for Ziegler–Nichols (theory.md §2). Derivative action is applied on the MEASUREMENT (not the error) with a low-pass filter, as in real flight controllers.

pid.description: PID gains for the roll attitude loop. C(s) = Kp + Ki/s + Kd·s.
pid.note: Fixed Kd = 0.04 with the Kp sweep [0.2..1.0] gives overshoot 1.18 / 10.85 / 18.65 / 24.54 / 29.16 % — crossing the 25 % comfort limit near Kp = 0.8. Because ζ·ωn = Kd/(2J) is fixed, the 2 % settling time stays 0.60 s across the whole sweep.

ziegler_nichols.description: Ultimate-cycle (closed-loop) tuning rules. Raise proportional gain on the rate loop until sustained oscillation: that gain is the ultimate gain Ku and the oscillation period is Pu. Then read the gains from a table.

classic.label: Classic Ziegler–Nichols (PID)
classic.note: Fast but AGGRESSIVE: quarter-amplitude decay gives ~68 % first overshoot on this plant. e_ss = 0 because of integral action. The PDF's '20 % overshoot' claim is incorrect for classic Z-N and is overridden here with the true simulated value.

tyreus_luyben.label: Tyreus–Luyben (robust PID)
tyreus_luyben.note: Raises Ti (gentler integral) and lowers Kp for robustness: overshoot drops to ~15 % (< 25 % target) with zero steady-state error. The practical 'refine the Z-N starting point' result.

ziegler_nichols.note: Ki = Kp/Ti, Kd = Kp·Td. td_factor for Tyreus–Luyben is 1/6.3 = 0.158730.

imu_presets.label: MPU-6000 (reference)
imu_presets.note: Reference 6-axis IMU running the estimator at the 400 Hz control rate. Over alpha ∈ {0.90,0.95,0.98,0.99} the drift+noise total is minimised at alpha = 0.98 (total ≈ 0.254°).

imu_presets.label: ICM-20602 (low-noise)
imu_presets.note: Lower bias and noise, 1 kHz ODR. Cleaner accel reference shifts the optimum toward a slightly lower alpha.

imu_presets.label: BMI270 (modern)
imu_presets.note: Modern low-drift sensor used on current flight stacks.

imu_presets.label: MPU-9250 (legacy)
imu_presets.note: Higher bias/noise legacy part; the filter must trust the gyro more (higher alpha) to suppress accel noise.

complementary_filter.description: First-order complementary filter fusing the integrated gyro rate (high-pass, drift-prone) with the accelerometer tilt angle (low-pass, noisy): theta = alpha·(theta + omega_gyro·dt) + (1−alpha)·theta_accel.
complementary_filter.note: Higher alpha trusts the gyro longer (more drift, less noise); lower alpha trusts the accel more (less drift, more noise). The total error is minimised at an interior optimum (alpha = 0.98 for the reference IMU). Pure gyro integration (alpha = 1) drifts without bound: 0.6°/s × 30 s = 18°.

disturbance.description: Constant disturbance torque used to demonstrate steady-state error. A horizontal CG offset d under gravity creates a couple Td = m·g·d that proportional action alone cannot null (e_ss = Td/Kp); integral action drives it to zero.
disturbance.note: Default Td = 0.5 kg × 9.80665 × 0.00357 m = 0.0175 N·m, using the CG offset from Experiment 2. e_ss(Kp): 0.2→5.01°, 0.6→1.67°, 1.0→1.00° (PD); → 0° once Ki > 0.

targets.note: A 'good tune' keeps overshoot under 25 %, settles quickly, and holds zero steady-state error against the disturbance torque.

constants.note: Shared lab constants, identical across all experiments.
